# Engage: How Did the Universe Form?

::: {.engage-box}
## 🌌 The Phenomenon

<div style="font-size: 1.3em; font-weight: 700; text-align: center; margin: 20px 0; text-shadow: 2px 2px 4px rgba(0,0,0,0.3);">
There are more stars in the universe than there are grains of sand on Earth, and scientists predict each one of those stars hosts several planets.
</div>

Where did all of those stars and planets come from? In this chapter you will use **light** from distant galaxies as evidence to figure out how the universe began, and whether other solar systems are likely to be like ours.
:::

```{ojs}
buildQuiz = function(id, title, questions) {
  const outer = html`<div id="${id}" style="margin:18px 0 24px 0;text-align:center;">

      display:inline-flex;align-items:center;gap:7px;

    >
      <span style="font-size:1.1em;">📝</span> ${title}
      <span class="chevron" style="transition:transform .3s;">▼</span>
    </button>
    <div class="quiz-body" style="
      max-height:0;opacity:0;overflow:hidden;
      transition:max-height .5s cubic-bezier(.4,0,.2,1),opacity .4s ease,margin-top .3s ease;
      margin-top:0;text-align:left;">
      <button class="close-btn" style="
        display:block;margin:0 auto 10px auto;
        background:rgba(102,126,234,.12);color:#667eea;border:none;
        padding:5px 18px;border-radius:50px;font-size:.85em;
        font-weight:600;cursor:pointer;">Hide Quiz</button>
      <p style="text-align:center;color:#718096;font-style:italic;font-size:.9em;margin-bottom:12px;">
        Select an answer for each question.</p>
    </div>
  </div>`;
  const toggle = outer.querySelector("button");
  const chevron = toggle.querySelector(".chevron");
  const body   = outer.querySelector(".quiz-body");
  const closeBtn = body.querySelector(".close-btn");
  function expand(){  body.style.maxHeight="2000px";body.style.opacity="1";body.style.marginTop="14px";chevron.style.transform="rotate(180deg)"; }
  function collapse(){ body.style.maxHeight="0";body.style.opacity="0";body.style.marginTop="0";chevron.style.transform="rotate(0)"; }
  toggle.onclick = () => body.style.maxHeight === "0px" || body.style.maxHeight === "" ? expand() : collapse();
  closeBtn.onclick = collapse;
  questions.forEach((qq, qi) => {
    const card = document.createElement("div");
    card.style.cssText = "background:#fff;color:#1e1b4b;border-radius:12px;padding:16px 20px;margin-bottom:14px;box-shadow:0 2px 8px rgba(0,0,0,.08);";
    card.innerHTML = `<p style="font-weight:700;margin:0 0 10px;">${qi+1}. ${qq.q}</p>`;
    qq.options.forEach((opt, oi) => {
      const btn = document.createElement("button");
      btn.textContent = opt;
      btn.style.cssText = "display:block;width:100%;min-height:44px;text-align:left;padding:10px 14px;margin:6px 0;border:2px solid #e2e8f0;border-radius:8px;background:#fff;color:#1e1b4b;cursor:pointer;font-size:.95em;transition:border-color .2s,background .2s;";
      btn.onmouseover = () => { if(!card.dataset.answered){ btn.style.borderColor="#667eea";btn.style.background="#f0f0ff"; }};
      btn.onmouseout  = () => { if(!card.dataset.answered){ btn.style.borderColor="#e2e8f0";btn.style.background="#fff"; }};
      btn.onclick = () => {
        if(card.dataset.answered) return;
        card.dataset.answered = "true";
        card.querySelectorAll("button").forEach(b => { b.style.cursor="default"; b.onmouseover=null; b.onmouseout=null; });
        if(oi === qq.correct){
          btn.style.borderColor="#48bb78";btn.style.background="#f0fff4";
          fb.innerHTML = "✅ Correct! " + qq.explanation;
          fb.style.color="#276749";fb.style.background="#f0fff4";
        } else {
          btn.style.borderColor="#fc8181";btn.style.background="#fff5f5";
          card.querySelectorAll("button")[qq.correct].style.borderColor="#48bb78";
          card.querySelectorAll("button")[qq.correct].style.background="#f0fff4";
          fb.innerHTML = "❌ " + qq.explanation;
          fb.style.color="#9b2c2c";fb.style.background="#fff5f5";
        }
        fb.style.padding="10px 14px";fb.style.marginTop="8px";
      };
      card.appendChild(btn);
    });
    const fb = document.createElement("div");
    fb.style.cssText = "border-radius:8px;font-size:.9em;transition:all .3s;";
    card.appendChild(fb);
    body.appendChild(card);
  });
  return outer;
}
```

# Explore: Investigating Light Spectra from Other Galaxies

::: {.explore-box}
## 🔭 Hubble Looks Beyond the Milky Way

In the 1920s, **Edwin Hubble** showed that some of the faint, fuzzy clouds of light in the sky are actually **entire galaxies**, much like our own Milky Way. The Milky Way is only one of many galaxies.

Hubble then studied the **light spectra** of these galaxies. A galaxy's spectrum is like a star's spectrum (which you analyzed in the stars investigation), except the light comes from an entire galaxy, not just one star.
:::

Below are the five spectra from your packet: three galaxies, a nearby star, and a **laboratory reference** of hydrogen and helium gas. The black lines are **absorption lines**. Their positions were measured from the packet image (to the nearest nanometer).

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
```


```{ojs}
//| echo: false
wlColor = function(nm) {
  // Approximate visible color for a wavelength in nanometers (after Dan Bruton)
  let r = 0, g = 0, b = 0;
  if (nm >= 380 && nm < 440) { r = -(nm - 440) / 60; b = 1; }
  else if (nm >= 440 && nm < 490) { g = (nm - 440) / 50; b = 1; }
  else if (nm >= 490 && nm < 510) { g = 1; b = -(nm - 510) / 20; }
  else if (nm >= 510 && nm < 580) { r = (nm - 510) / 70; g = 1; }
  else if (nm >= 580 && nm < 645) { r = 1; g = -(nm - 645) / 65; }
  else if (nm >= 645 && nm <= 780) { r = 1; }
  else return "#3a3a3a";
  let f = 1;
  if (nm < 420) f = 0.35 + 0.65 * (nm - 380) / 40;
  else if (nm > 700) f = 0.35 + 0.65 * (780 - nm) / 80;
  const c = v => Math.round(255 * Math.pow(v * f, 0.8));
  return `rgb(${c(r)},${c(g)},${c(b)})`;
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
spectrumSvg = function({rows, lo = 386, hi = 716, refLines = null, showRef = false, arrowIndex = null, gradId = "ou-grad"}) {
  const W = 720, labelW = width < 520 ? 130 : 170, rowH = 34, gap = 12, top = 10;
  const H = top + rows.length * (rowH + gap) + 40;
  const x = d3.scaleLinear([lo, hi], [labelW, W - 12]);
  const svg = d3.create("svg").attr("viewBox", `0 0 ${W} ${H}`)
    .style("width", "100%").style("height", "auto").style("max-width", "760px")
    .style("display", "block").style("margin", "auto").style("background", "#8e9296").style("border-radius", "10px");
  const grad = svg.append("defs").append("linearGradient").attr("id", gradId).attr("x1", "0%").attr("x2", "100%");
  d3.range(0, 1.0001, 0.02).forEach(t => grad.append("stop").attr("offset", `${t * 100}%`)
    .attr("stop-color", wlColor(Math.max(381, Math.min(779, lo + t * (hi - lo))))));
  rows.forEach((row, i) => {
    const y = top + i * (rowH + gap);
    svg.append("text").attr("x", labelW - 8).attr("y", y + rowH / 2 + 5).attr("text-anchor", "end")
      .attr("font-size", 15).attr("font-weight", 700).attr("fill", "#111").text(row.label);
    svg.append("rect").attr("x", labelW).attr("y", y).attr("width", W - 12 - labelW).attr("height", rowH).attr("fill", `url(#${gradId})`);
    row.lines.forEach((l, j) => {
      if (l < lo || l > hi) return;
      const w = j === 0 ? 7 : 3;
      svg.append("rect").attr("x", x(l) - w / 2).attr("y", y).attr("width", w).attr("height", rowH).attr("fill", "#000")
        .append("title").text(`${row.label}: line at about ${l} nm`);
    });
    if (showRef && refLines) refLines.forEach(l => {
      svg.append("line").attr("x1", x(l)).attr("x2", x(l)).attr("y1", y - 3).attr("y2", y + rowH + 3)
        .attr("stroke", "#fff").attr("stroke-width", 1.5).attr("stroke-dasharray", "3,3");
    });
    if (arrowIndex != null && refLines && row.lines[arrowIndex] != null && row.lines[arrowIndex] !== refLines[arrowIndex]) {
      const x1 = x(refLines[arrowIndex]), x2 = x(row.lines[arrowIndex]);
      svg.append("line").attr("x1", x1).attr("x2", x2).attr("y1", y + rowH + 5).attr("y2", y + rowH + 5)
        .attr("stroke", "#111").attr("stroke-width", 2.5);
      const dir = x2 > x1 ? 1 : -1;
      svg.append("path").attr("d", `M${x2},${y + rowH + 5} l${-8 * dir},-5 l0,10 z`).attr("fill", "#111");
    }
  });
  const axY = top + rows.length * (rowH + gap);
  d3.range(Math.ceil(lo / 100) * 100, hi + 1, 100).forEach(t => {
    svg.append("line").attr("x1", x(t)).attr("x2", x(t)).attr("y1", axY - gap + 2).attr("y2", axY + 2).attr("stroke", "#111");
    svg.append("text").attr("x", x(t)).attr("y", axY + 16).attr("text-anchor", "middle").attr("font-size", 14).attr("fill", "#111").text(t);
  });
  svg.append("text").attr("x", (labelW + W) / 2).attr("y", axY + 34).attr("text-anchor", "middle")
    .attr("font-size", 15).attr("font-weight", 700).attr("fill", "#111").text("Wavelength (nm)");
  return svg.node();
}
```

```{ojs}
    Plot.ruleX([0])
  ]
```

::: {.key-idea}
### 💡 What the spectra show

- **Same pattern:** every spectrum has the **same pattern** of lines (same spacing, thick line first). That pattern is the fingerprint of **hydrogen and helium**, so the galaxies contain the same elements as the lab sample.
- **Different position:** the whole pattern is **shifted toward longer (redder) wavelengths**. The star shifts a little, the nearby galaxy more, the distant galaxy more, and the very distant galaxy the most (two of its lines are pushed past the red end of the chart).
- **Relationship:** the **farther** the galaxy, the **bigger the shift toward red**.
:::

## Waves: Wavelength and Frequency

Light and sound are both forms of **energy** that travel from a **source** (like a star) to an **observer** (like us) as **waves**.

- **Wavelength** = the distance from one peak to the next.
- **Frequency** = how many peaks pass by each second.
- **Short wavelength ↔ high frequency. Long wavelength ↔ low frequency.** You can see this in the wave tool in Model 2 below.

::: {.student-task}
### ✏️ In your packet: High and low frequency waves

1. Based on the high- and low-frequency wave image, how are **frequency and wavelength** related?
2. Looking back at the galaxy spectra, how does the **distance** of a galaxy relate to the **frequency** of the light coming from it? (Hint: the lines moved to **longer** wavelengths.)
:::

## Model 1: Sound Waves from a Moving Source

To make sense of the shifted lines, start with **sound**, which behaves like light but is easier to notice. Think of an ambulance siren: it sounds **higher** as it comes toward you and **lower** as it drives away. This is the **Doppler effect**.

In this model the **blue dot** is the source. It gives off a sound wave (a circle) at a **steady rate** while it moves left to right. The **receiver** (microphone) turns **green** each time a wave passes through it.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
dopplerSim = function({mode = "sound", speed = 0.5, motion = "right", audio = false, invalidation}) {
  const W = 700, H = mode === "sound" ? 210 : 230;
  const c = 130;                 // wave speed (pixels per second)
  const emitEvery = 0.32;        // seconds between waves at the source
  const v = speed * c;
  const svg = d3.create("svg").attr("viewBox", `0 0 ${W} ${H}`)
    .style("width", "100%").style("height", "auto").style("max-width", "760px")
    .style("display", "block").style("margin", "auto").style("border-radius", "10px")
    .style("touch-action", "pan-y");
  svg.append("rect").attr("width", W).attr("height", H).attr("rx", 10)
    .attr("fill", mode === "sound" ? "#f8fafc" : "#05051a").attr("stroke", "#94a3b8");
  const clip = svg.append("defs").append("clipPath").attr("id", `ou-clip-${mode}`);
  clip.append("rect").attr("width", W).attr("height", H).attr("rx", 10);
  const waveG = svg.append("g").attr("clip-path", `url(#ou-clip-${mode})`);
  const waveColor = mode === "sound" ? "#334155" : "#cbd5e1";

  // Layout
  let srcY, rx, ry, startX, endX;
  if (mode === "sound") { srcY = 85; rx = 470; ry = 130; startX = 40; endX = 660; }
  else { srcY = 105; rx = 70; ry = 105;
    startX = motion === "toward" ? 620 : motion === "away" ? 260 : 450;
    endX = motion === "toward" ? 230 : motion === "away" ? 660 : 450; }
  const dirSign = endX > startX ? 1 : endX < startX ? -1 : 0;

  // Receiver / observer
  const recv = svg.append("g");
  let recvMark;
  if (mode === "sound") {
    recv.append("rect").attr("x", rx - 4).attr("y", ry).attr("width", 8).attr("height", 16).attr("rx", 3).attr("fill", "#334155");
    recvMark = recv.append("circle").attr("cx", rx).attr("cy", ry).attr("r", 7).attr("fill", "#334155");
    svg.append("text").attr("x", rx).attr("y", ry + 34).attr("text-anchor", "middle").attr("font-size", 12).attr("fill", "#334155").text("Receiver");
  } else {
    recvMark = recv.append("circle").attr("cx", rx).attr("cy", ry).attr("r", 12).attr("fill", "#4fa3e0");
    svg.append("text").attr("x", rx).attr("y", ry + 30).attr("text-anchor", "middle").attr("font-size", 12).attr("fill", "#e2e8f0").text("Earth");
  }
  const src = svg.append("circle").attr("r", mode === "sound" ? 7 : 11).attr("fill", mode === "sound" ? "#1d4ed8" : "#ffffff").attr("cy", srcY);
  const srcLabel = svg.append("text").attr("text-anchor", "middle").attr("font-size", 12)
    .attr("fill", mode === "sound" ? "#1d4ed8" : "#e2e8f0").attr("y", srcY - 18).text(mode === "sound" ? "Source" : "Galaxy");
  svg.append("rect").attr("x", 6).attr("y", H - 50).attr("width", W - 12).attr("height", 44).attr("rx", 6)
    .attr("fill", mode === "sound" ? "rgba(248,250,252,0.88)" : "rgba(5,5,26,0.85)");
  const readout = svg.append("text").attr("x", 14).attr("y", H - 30).attr("font-size", 14).attr("font-weight", 700)
    .attr("fill", mode === "sound" ? "#0f172a" : "#e2e8f0");
  const readout2 = svg.append("text").attr("x", 14).attr("y", H - 10).attr("font-size", 13)
    .attr("fill", mode === "sound" ? "#334155" : "#cbd5e1");

  let ctx = null;
  function click() {
    if (!audio) return;
    try {
      ctx = ctx || new (window.AudioContext || window.webkitAudioContext)();
      const o = ctx.createOscillator(), g = ctx.createGain();
      o.type = "triangle"; o.frequency.value = 180;
      g.gain.setValueAtTime(0.25, ctx.currentTime);
      g.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(0.001, ctx.currentTime + 0.08);
      o.connect(g).connect(ctx.destination); o.start(); o.stop(ctx.currentTime + 0.09);
    } catch (e) {}
  }

  let waves = [], arrivals = [], t = 0, lastEmit = -1, flash = 0, raf = 0, last = performance.now();
  let cycleStart = 0;
  const travelTime = dirSign === 0 ? 8 : Math.abs(endX - startX) / Math.max(v, 1e-6);
  const cycle = dirSign === 0 || v === 0 ? 8 : Math.min(travelTime, 30) + 1.5;

  function step(ts) {
    const dt = Math.min((ts - last) / 1000, 0.05); last = ts; t += dt;
    let local = t - cycleStart;
    if (local > cycle) { cycleStart = t; local = 0; waves = []; arrivals = []; lastEmit = -1; }
    const moving = local < travelTime;
    const sx = startX + dirSign * v * Math.min(local, travelTime);
    if (moving && (lastEmit < 0 || t - lastEmit >= emitEvery)) { waves.push({x: sx, y: srcY, t0: t, hit: false}); lastEmit = t; }
    waves.forEach(w => {
      const r = c * (t - w.t0);
      if (!w.hit && r >= Math.hypot(rx - w.x, ry - w.y)) { w.hit = true; arrivals.push(t); flash = 0.12; click(); }
    });
    waves = waves.filter(w => c * (t - w.t0) < 900);
    src.attr("cx", sx); srcLabel.attr("x", sx);
    waveG.selectAll("circle").data(waves).join("circle")
      .attr("cx", w => w.x).attr("cy", w => w.y).attr("r", w => c * (t - w.t0))
      .attr("fill", "none").attr("stroke", waveColor).attr("stroke-width", 1.4).attr("stroke-opacity", w => Math.max(0.15, 1 - c * (t - w.t0) / 900));
    flash = Math.max(0, flash - dt);
    if (mode === "sound") recvMark.attr("fill", flash > 0 ? "#22c55e" : "#334155");
    const fEmit = 1 / emitEvery;
    if (arrivals.length >= 2) {
      const fObs = 1 / (arrivals[arrivals.length - 1] - arrivals[arrivals.length - 2]);
      const ratio = fObs / fEmit;
      const word = ratio > 1.03 ? (mode === "sound" ? "HIGHER pitch" : "HIGHER frequency") : ratio < 0.97 ? (mode === "sound" ? "LOWER pitch" : "LOWER frequency") : "no change";
      readout.text(`Receiver detects ${fObs.toFixed(1)} waves/s → ${word}`);
    } else readout.text("Waiting for waves to reach the receiver…");
    readout2.text(`Source gives off ${fEmit.toFixed(1)} waves/s (constant). Source speed = ${(speed * 100).toFixed(0)}% of wave speed.`);
    raf = requestAnimationFrame(step);
  }
  raf = requestAnimationFrame(step);
  if (invalidation) invalidation.then(() => { cancelAnimationFrame(raf); if (ctx) try { ctx.close(); } catch (e) {} });
  return svg.node();
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof soundSpeed = Inputs.range([0, 0.8], {label: "Source speed (fraction of sound speed):", step: 0.05, value: 0.5})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof soundOn = Inputs.toggle({label: "🔊 Snare click at the receiver", value: false})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
dopplerSim({mode: "sound", speed: soundSpeed, motion: "right", audio: soundOn, invalidation})
```

::: {.key-idea}
### 💡 What Model 1 shows

- The source makes waves at a **constant** rate the whole time.
- While the source moves **toward** the receiver, the waves in front of it get **squeezed together** (shorter wavelength), so they arrive **more often**: **higher frequency → higher pitch**.
- After the source passes and moves **away**, the waves behind it are **stretched apart** (longer wavelength), so they arrive **less often**: **lower frequency → lower pitch**.
- The wave **energy spreads out** over bigger and bigger circles as it travels; it isn't destroyed.
:::

::: {.student-task}
### ✏️ In your packet: Siren and Model 1

- Listen to the **Siren Doppler Effect** video: what happens to the sound? What are your initial ideas to explain it?
- **Model 1:** What happens to the **energy** in the sound wave over time? With the snare muted, **snap your fingers** each time the blue dot makes a wave: is the rate faster, slower, or constant?
- Unmute and watch the receiver: How often do waves come out of the blue dot? How does the sound at the microphone change as the dot moves? Why?
:::

## Model 2: Pitch and Wavelength

Tap a piano key to play a note and see its sound wave. The graph always shows the same short slice of time (10 milliseconds), so you can compare how many peaks fit in.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof pianoFreq = {
  const notes = [["C4", 262], ["D4", 294], ["E4", 330], ["F4", 349], ["G4", 392], ["A4", 440], ["B4", 494], ["C5", 523]];
  const wrap = html`<div style="display:flex;gap:4px;justify-content:center;flex-wrap:nowrap;max-width:560px;margin:8px auto;"></div>`;
  let ctx = null;
  wrap.value = 262;
  notes.forEach(([name, f]) => {
    const b = document.createElement("button");
    b.innerHTML = `<span style="display:block;font-weight:700;">${name}</span><span style="font-size:.75em;">${f} Hz</span>`;
    b.style.cssText = "flex:1;min-width:0;min-height:96px;border:2px solid #334155;border-radius:0 0 8px 8px;background:#fff;color:#0f172a;cursor:pointer;padding:4px 2px;display:flex;flex-direction:column;justify-content:flex-end;";
    b.onclick = () => {
      wrap.value = f;
      wrap.querySelectorAll("button").forEach(x => x.style.background = "#fff");
      b.style.background = "#ffe082";
      try {
        ctx = ctx || new (window.AudioContext || window.webkitAudioContext)();
        const o = ctx.createOscillator(), g = ctx.createGain();
        o.frequency.value = f; g.gain.setValueAtTime(0.15, ctx.currentTime);
        g.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(0.001, ctx.currentTime + 0.6);
        o.connect(g).connect(ctx.destination); o.start(); o.stop(ctx.currentTime + 0.6);
      } catch (e) {}
      wrap.dispatchEvent(new Event("input", {bubbles: true}));
    };
    if (f === 262) b.style.background = "#ffe082";
    wrap.appendChild(b);
  });
  return wrap;
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  const f = pianoFreq;
  const pts = d3.range(0, 10.0001, 0.02).map(ms => ({ms, y: Math.sin(2 * Math.PI * f * ms / 1000)}));
  const wavelength = 343 / f;
  return Plot.plot({
    title: `Sound wave: ${f} Hz`,
    subtitle: `${(f / 100).toFixed(1)} peaks in 10 ms · wavelength in air = 343 m/s ÷ ${f} Hz ≈ ${wavelength.toFixed(2)} m`,
    width: width, height: 220, marginLeft: 40, marginBottom: 40,
    x: {label: "Time (milliseconds)", domain: [0, 10]},
    y: {label: null, domain: [-1.2, 1.2], ticks: 0},
    marks: [Plot.ruleY([0], {stroke: "#94a3b8"}), Plot.line(pts, {x: "ms", y: "y", stroke: "#00a8a3", strokeWidth: 2.5})]
  });
}
```

```{ojs}
    options: ["Higher pitch, and the wavelength gets shorter", "Higher pitch, and the wavelength gets longer", "Lower pitch, and the wavelength gets shorter", "Nothing changes"],
    correct: 0,
    explanation: "More peaks fit into the same time, so the peaks are closer together. C4 (262 Hz) has a wavelength of about 1.31 m; C5 (523 Hz) about 0.66 m."
  },
```

::: {.key-idea}
### 💡 Explaining the siren

From **Model 1**: when the source moves toward you, the waves you receive have a **higher frequency**; when it moves away, a **lower frequency**.
From **Model 2**: **higher frequency = higher pitch**.
So the siren sounds higher as it approaches and lower as it drives away, even though the siren itself never changes its sound. The **driver** inside the ambulance moves with the source, so for them there is no Doppler effect: they hear the same pitch the whole time.
:::

```{ojs}

dopplerSim({mode: "light", speed: galaxyMotion === "Not moving" ? 0 : galaxySpeed,
  motion: galaxyMotion === "Moving toward Earth" ? "toward" : galaxyMotion === "Moving away from Earth" ? "away" : "none", invalidation})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  const emitted = 550;
  const vr = galaxyMotion === "Moving away from Earth" ? galaxySpeed : galaxyMotion === "Moving toward Earth" ? -galaxySpeed : 0;
  const observed = emitted * (1 + vr);
  const freqWord = vr > 0 ? "Decrease" : vr < 0 ? "Increase" : "No change";
  const shiftWord = vr > 0 ? "Shift toward RED (redshift)" : vr < 0 ? "Shift toward BLUE (blueshift)" : "No shift";
  const box = d3.create("div").style("display", "flex").style("flex-wrap", "wrap").style("gap", "12px").style("justify-content", "center").style("margin", "10px 0");
  const swatch = (label, nm) => box.append("div").style("text-align", "center").style("min-width", "130px").html(
    `<div style="width:110px;height:60px;margin:auto;border-radius:10px;border:2px solid #334155;background:${wlColor(Math.min(779, Math.max(381, nm)))}"></div>` +
    `<div style="font-size:.85em;margin-top:4px;"><strong>${label}</strong><br>${nm.toFixed(0)} nm</div>`);
  swatch("Light given off", emitted);
  swatch("Light seen on Earth", observed);
  box.append("div").style("flex", "1 1 220px").style("padding", "10px 14px").style("border-radius", "10px")
    .style("background", vr > 0 ? "rgba(231,76,60,.12)" : vr < 0 ? "rgba(52,152,219,.14)" : "rgba(148,163,184,.18)")
    .html(`<strong>Change in frequency on Earth:</strong> ${freqWord}<br><strong>Change of color:</strong> ${shiftWord}<br><span style="font-size:.85em;">Wavelength seen = ${emitted} nm × (1 ${vr >= 0 ? "+" : "−"} ${Math.abs(vr).toFixed(2)}) ≈ ${observed.toFixed(0)} nm</span>`);
  return box.node();
}
```

## Model 4: Color, Wavelength, and Frequency

Why does the model show the shifted light as **red** or **blue**? Slide through the visible spectrum. The color names and boundaries use the packet's *Portion of Electromagnetic Spectrum* chart.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof emNm = Inputs.range([380, 750], {label: "Wavelength (nm):", step: 1, value: 550})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  const nm = emNm;
  const name = nm < 400 ? "Ultraviolet (invisible)" : nm < 430 ? "Violet" : nm < 490 ? "Blue" : nm < 530 ? "Green" : nm < 580 ? "Yellow" : nm < 630 ? "Orange" : nm <= 700 ? "Red" : "Infrared (invisible)";
  const freq = 3e8 / (nm * 1e-9);
  const bands = [
    {name: "Violet", lo: 400, hi: 430}, {name: "Blue", lo: 430, hi: 490}, {name: "Green", lo: 490, hi: 530},
    {name: "Yellow", lo: 530, hi: 580}, {name: "Orange", lo: 580, hi: 630}, {name: "Red", lo: 630, hi: 700}
  ];
  const wrap = d3.create("div");
  wrap.append(() => Plot.plot({
    width: width, height: 130, marginLeft: 10, marginRight: 10, marginBottom: 36,
    x: {domain: [380, 750], label: "Wavelength (nm) → longer wavelength, lower frequency, lower energy"},
    y: {axis: null, domain: [0, 1]},
    marks: [
      Plot.rectY(d3.range(380, 750, 2), {x1: d => d, x2: d => d + 2, y1: 0.35, y2: 1, fill: d => wlColor(d + 1)}),
      Plot.text(bands, {x: d => (d.lo + d.hi) / 2, y: 0.18, text: d => width < 500 ? d.name[0] : d.name, fontSize: 11}),
      Plot.ruleX([400, 430, 490, 530, 580, 630, 700], {y1: 0, y2: 0.35, stroke: "#64748b"}),
      Plot.ruleX([nm], {stroke: "#111", strokeWidth: 3}),
      Plot.dot([nm], {x: d => d, y: 1, r: 7, fill: "#111"})
    ]
  }));
  wrap.append("div").style("display", "flex").style("gap", "14px").style("align-items", "center").style("flex-wrap", "wrap").style("margin", "6px 0 0")
    .html(`<div style="width:64px;height:44px;border-radius:8px;border:2px solid #334155;background:${wlColor(nm)}"></div>
      <div><strong>${name}</strong> · wavelength ${nm} nm = ${(nm / 100).toFixed(2)} × 10² nm · frequency ≈ ${(freq / 1e14).toFixed(2)} × 10¹⁴ Hz</div>`);
  return wrap.node();
}
```

::: {.key-idea}
### 💡 Colors of light

- **Violet and blue** light have the **shortest wavelengths** and **highest frequencies** (about 7.7 × 10¹⁴ Hz at 400 nm).
- **Red** light has the **longest wavelengths** and **lowest frequencies** (about 4.3 × 10¹⁴ Hz at 700 nm).
- So light from a galaxy moving **toward** us is squeezed toward **blue** (blueshift), and light from a galaxy moving **away** is stretched toward **red** (redshift).
:::

```{ojs}
    correct: 1,

  }
])
```

# Explain: What Does the Light Spectra of Galaxies Tell Us?

::: {.explain-box}
## 🧠 Using the Doppler Effect as Evidence

Studying the light from an object tells us whether it is moving **away** from us, **toward** us, or **not moving**. Now use that idea to make **predictions**. A prediction is not a guess: you justify it with the Doppler effect.
:::

Pick a scenario to see what the spectrum of a distant galaxy **would look like** if that scenario were true.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof predScenario = Inputs.radio(["The universe is expanding", "The universe is contracting", "The universe is static"], {label: "Scenario:", value: "The universe is expanding"})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  const s = predScenario.includes("expanding") ? 45 : predScenario.includes("contracting") ? -45 : 0;
  const node = d3.create("div");
  node.append(() => spectrumSvg({
    rows: [{label: "Predicted galaxy", lines: labLines.map(l => l + s)}, {label: "Lab reference", lines: labLines}],
    lo: 340, hi: 760, refLines: labLines, showRef: true, arrowIndex: s === 0 ? null : 3, gradId: "ou-grad-pred"
  }));
  const claim = s > 0
    ? ["If the universe is expanding, I'd expect the light to shift toward the <strong>red</strong> end of the spectrum",
       "because the source is moving away from Earth, resulting in <strong>longer</strong> wavelengths and <strong>lower</strong> frequency light",
       "and light with <strong>longer</strong> wavelengths appears <strong>red</strong>."]
    : s < 0
    ? ["If the universe is contracting, I'd expect the light to shift toward the <strong>blue</strong> end of the spectrum",
       "because the source is moving toward Earth, resulting in <strong>shorter</strong> wavelengths and <strong>higher</strong> frequency light",
       "and light with <strong>shorter</strong> wavelengths appears <strong>blue</strong>."]
    : ["If the universe is static, I'd expect <strong>no shift</strong>: the lines would match the lab reference",
       "because the source is not moving toward or away from Earth, so the wavelength and frequency <strong>do not change</strong>",
       "and the same wavelengths appear the same color."];
  node.append("div").style("display", "grid").style("grid-template-columns", "repeat(auto-fit, minmax(190px, 1fr))").style("gap", "8px").style("margin-top", "10px")
    .html(["Claim", "Evidence", "Reasoning"].map((h, i) =>
      `<div style="border:1px solid #94a3b8;border-radius:8px;padding:10px;"><div style="font-weight:800;margin-bottom:4px;">${h}</div>${claim[i]}</div>`).join(""));
  return node.node();
}
```

::: {.key-idea}
### 💡 The universe is expanding

**Universe: static, contracting, or expanding?** If galaxies were moving away from us, the wavelengths would become **longer**, so the absorption lines would move toward the **red** end.

That's exactly what the packet's spectra show: **every galaxy's lines are redshifted**, and the **farther** the galaxy, the **larger** the redshift. Galaxies are moving away from us, and farther ones are moving away faster. The best explanation is that **space itself is expanding**, carrying galaxies apart from each other in every direction.
:::

## ➕ Optional Extension: Hubble's Law

In 1929 Hubble also measured how **fast** galaxies are moving away. Farther galaxies recede **faster**, in a straight-line relationship now called **Hubble's Law**: $v = H_0 \times d$, with $H_0 \approx 70$ km/s per megaparsec (1 Mpc ≈ 3.26 million light-years). The data below are approximate modern values for some well-known galaxy clusters.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
hubbleData = [
  {name: "Virgo Cluster", d: 16.5, v: 1100},
  {name: "Fornax Cluster", d: 19, v: 1380},
  {name: "Hydra Cluster", d: 54, v: 3780},
  {name: "Perseus Cluster", d: 75, v: 5370},
  {name: "Coma Cluster", d: 99, v: 6930},
  {name: "Abell 2029", d: 330, v: 23200}
]
```

```{ojs}

  title: "Hubble's Law: farther galaxies move away faster",
  subtitle: "Dashed line: v = 70 × d",
  width: width, height: 340, marginLeft: 60, marginBottom: 42, marginRight: 20,
  x: {label: "Distance (Mpc)", grid: true, domain: [0, 350]},
  y: {label: "Speed moving away (km/s)", grid: true, domain: [0, 25000]},
  marks: [
    Plot.line([[0, 0], [350, 24500]], {stroke: "#00a8a3", strokeDasharray: "6,4", strokeWidth: 2}),
    Plot.dot(hubbleData, {x: "d", y: "v", r: 7, fill: "#e74c3c", stroke: "#333", tip: true, title: d => `${d.name}\n${d.d} Mpc\n${d.v.toLocaleString()} km/s`}),
    Plot.text(hubbleData.filter(d => d.d > 50), {x: "d", y: "v", text: "name", dy: -14, fontSize: 10})
  ]
})
```

# Elaborate: How Did It All Start?

::: {.elaborate-box}
## 🎈 Running the Expansion Backward

The universe is expanding! So what was it like **in the past**? In class you use a **balloon** to model space: draw galaxies (with light waves) on it, then inflate and deflate it. The model below works the same way.
:::

## Part 1: What Did the Universe Look Like in the Past?

Drag the slider to go **back in time**. The galaxies stay the same size; it's the **space between them** (the balloon) that changes. The squiggles are light waves traveling through that space.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
ouScale = function(gyrAgo) {
  // Relative size of the universe compared with today (simplified expansion model, age 13.7 billion years)
  const age = 13.7, k = 0.0899, t = age - gyrAgo;
  if (t <= 0) return 0;
  return Math.pow(Math.sinh(k * t) / Math.sinh(k * age), 2 / 3);
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof balloonAgo = Inputs.range([0, 13.7], {label: "Billions of years ago:", step: 0.1, value: 0})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  const a = ouScale(balloonAgo);
  const W = 640, H = 400, cx = W / 2, cy = 190, R0 = 170;
  let s = 7; const rand = () => { s = (s * 16807) % 2147483647; return s / 2147483647; };
  const gal = d3.range(18).map(i => { const r = 0.88 * Math.sqrt(rand()), th = 2 * Math.PI * rand(); return {x: r * Math.cos(th), y: r * Math.sin(th), tilt: rand() * 180}; });
  const svg = d3.create("svg").attr("viewBox", `0 0 ${W} ${H}`).style("width", "100%").style("height", "auto")
    .style("max-width", "640px").style("display", "block").style("margin", "auto");
  svg.append("rect").attr("width", W).attr("height", H).attr("rx", 12).attr("fill", "#0b0b24");
  const R = Math.max(R0 * a, 2);
  const T = a > 0 ? 2.725 / a : Infinity;
  const glow = a < 0.02 ? "#fff3b0" : a < 0.1 ? "#ffb74d" : "#e57373";
  svg.append("circle").attr("cx", cx).attr("cy", cy).attr("r", R).attr("fill", glow).attr("fill-opacity", a < 0.05 ? 0.9 : 0.25).attr("stroke", "#ef9a9a").attr("stroke-width", 2);
  if (a > 0.04) {
    gal.forEach((g, i) => {
      const gx = cx + g.x * R, gy = cy + g.y * R;
      const lam = 9 * a;  // wavelength of the drawn light stretches with space
      const pts = d3.range(0, 3 * 2 * Math.PI + 0.01, 0.3).map(p => [gx + 9 + (p / (2 * Math.PI)) * lam, gy + 4 * Math.sin(p)]);
      svg.append("path").attr("d", d3.line()(pts)).attr("fill", "none").attr("stroke", "#fff59d").attr("stroke-width", 1.2);
      svg.append("ellipse").attr("cx", gx).attr("cy", gy).attr("rx", 6).attr("ry", 2.6).attr("transform", `rotate(${g.tilt},${gx},${gy})`)
        .attr("fill", i === 0 || i === 1 ? "#4fc3f7" : "#ffffff");
    });
    const A = gal[0], B = gal[1];
    svg.append("line").attr("x1", cx + A.x * R).attr("y1", cy + A.y * R).attr("x2", cx + B.x * R).attr("y2", cy + B.y * R)
      .attr("stroke", "#4fc3f7").attr("stroke-dasharray", "4,3");
  }
  const lines = balloonAgo >= 13.7
    ? ["The beginning of time: all of space is squeezed to a tiny point.", "Extremely hot and dense: no atoms, no stars, no galaxies yet."]
    : [`Size of the universe: ${(a * 100).toFixed(a < 0.1 ? 1 : 0)}% of today · distance between the blue galaxies: ${(a * 100).toFixed(a < 0.1 ? 1 : 0)}% of today`,
       `Light traveling since then gets stretched ${(1 / a).toFixed(1)}× · temperature of the leftover radiation: ${T < 1000 ? T.toFixed(1) : Math.round(T).toLocaleString()} K`];
  svg.append("text").attr("x", W / 2).attr("y", 26).attr("text-anchor", "middle").attr("fill", "white").attr("font-size", 16).attr("font-weight", 700)
    .text(balloonAgo === 0 ? "The universe today (13.7 billion years after the beginning)" : `The universe ${balloonAgo.toFixed(1)} billion years ago`);
  lines.forEach((l, i) => svg.append("text").attr("x", W / 2).attr("y", H - 34 + i * 20).attr("text-anchor", "middle").attr("fill", "#cbd5e1").attr("font-size", 12.5).text(l));
  if (a > 0 && a <= 0.04) svg.append("text").attr("x", W / 2).attr("y", cy + R + 22).attr("text-anchor", "middle").attr("fill", "#fff3b0").attr("font-size", 12)
    .text("Too early for galaxies: matter is packed together, hot and glowing");
  return svg.node();
}
```

## Parts 2 and 3: Conditions of the Early Universe and Testing the Theory

Squeeze all the stars and galaxies of the universe together and you get something **extremely dense and extremely hot**. As it expanded, it **cooled down** and spread out.

- At first it was **so hot and dense that no elements could exist**, only subatomic particles, as if all the elements had melted apart.
- As it expanded and cooled, subatomic particles could **fuse** into the first atoms, like water droplets forming from steam. That window was **short**, because the particles were quickly spreading apart and cooling too much to fuse.
- For that short time the universe behaved like the **core of a star**, making only **light elements**.

::: {.key-idea}
### 💡 Two conclusions from computational models

**Claim 1:** When matter formed into elements, **only hydrogen and helium** formed: **75% hydrogen and 25% helium** by mass.

**Claim 2:** Like the core of a hot star made of hydrogen and helium, the early universe gave off a **huge amount of energy as visible light**.
:::

**How are we confident in this explanation?** Scientists only call something a **theory** if it stands up to repeated testing. For the Big Bang, astronomers:

1. used observations of the **expanding universe** to predict that it started off very small,
2. used **computational models** to predict the conditions of the early universe,
3. used how **energy and matter** behave to predict what we should observe **today**, and
4. **compared** today's observations with those predictions.

::: {.callout-important}
## Law of Conservation of Matter and Energy

Within a closed system, matter and energy can **change form**, but the **total amount of matter and energy is constant**.
:::

So if the Big Bang is right, we should still find (1) the **hydrogen and helium** it made, and (2) its **light energy**, still traveling through space but **stretched** by 13.7 billion years of expansion.

### The light stretcher

The early universe glowed like a hot star at about **3,000 K**. At 1× its brightest wavelength is just past red, but a big part of the glow is visible red-orange light, like a cool red star. Stretch space and watch what happens to that glow. The regions below use the packet's *Portion of Electromagnetic Spectrum* chart.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof stretchFactor = Inputs.range([1, 1100], {label: "Times space has stretched:", step: 1, value: 1, transform: Math.log})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  const T = 3000 / stretchFactor;
  const hck = 1.4388e7; // nm·K
  const xs = d3.range(1, 9.3, 0.01).map(e => 10 ** e);
  const raw = xs.map(l => ({l, y: (1 / l ** 4) / (Math.exp(hck / (l * T)) - 1)}));
  const max = d3.max(raw, d => d.y);
  const curve = raw.map(d => ({l: d.l, y: d.y / max}));
  const peak = 2.898e6 / T;
  const region = peak < 400 ? "ultraviolet" : peak <= 700 ? "visible light" : peak < 1e6 ? "infrared" : "microwaves";
  const regions = [
    {name: "Ultraviolet", lo: 10, hi: 400, fill: "#b39ddb"},
    {name: "Visible", lo: 400, hi: 700, fill: "#fff176"},
    {name: "Infrared", lo: 700, hi: 1e6, fill: "#ef9a9a"},
    {name: "Microwaves", lo: 1e6, hi: 1e9, fill: "#90caf9"}
  ];
  const fmtNm = v => v < 1e3 ? `${v.toFixed(0)} nm` : v < 1e6 ? `${(v / 1e3).toFixed(1)} µm` : `${(v / 1e6).toFixed(2)} mm`;
  return Plot.plot({
    title: `Glow of the early universe, stretched ${stretchFactor.toFixed(0)}×`,
    subtitle: `Temperature ≈ ${T < 100 ? T.toFixed(1) : Math.round(T).toLocaleString()} K · brightest wavelength ≈ ${fmtNm(peak)} (${region})`,
    width: width, height: 300, marginLeft: 20, marginBottom: 44, marginRight: 14,
    x: {type: "log", label: "Wavelength (nm, log scale) → longer wavelength, lower energy", domain: [10, 1e9], tickFormat: d => { const e = Math.log10(d); return Number.isInteger(Math.round(e * 1000) / 1000) && e % 2 === 0 ? `10^${e}` : ""; }},
    y: {axis: null, domain: [0, 1.25]},
    marks: [
      Plot.rect(regions, {x1: "lo", x2: "hi", y1: 0, y2: 1.25, fill: "fill", fillOpacity: 0.35}),
      Plot.text(regions, {x: d => Math.sqrt(d.lo * d.hi), y: 1.17, text: d => width < 520 && d.name === "Visible" ? "Vis." : d.name, fontSize: 11, fontWeight: 700}),
      Plot.areaY(curve, {x: "l", y: "y", fill: "#e65100", fillOpacity: 0.55}),
      Plot.line(curve, {x: "l", y: "y", stroke: "#bf360c", strokeWidth: 2}),
      Plot.ruleX([peak], {stroke: "#111", strokeDasharray: "4,3"})
    ]
  });
}
```

## Part 4: Compare Your Predictions to Observations Today

### Evidence 1: The matter

Using the absorption spectra of stars, astronomers observe that across the universe matter is **slightly less than 75% hydrogen, slightly less than 25% helium, and about 2% other elements** by mass. The packet's pie charts compare the prediction with an observed breakdown:

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
compositionData = [
  {chart: "Early universe (predicted)", element: "Hydrogen", pct: 75},
  {chart: "Early universe (predicted)", element: "Helium", pct: 25},
  {chart: "Universe today (observed)", element: "Hydrogen", pct: 70},
  {chart: "Universe today (observed)", element: "Helium", pct: 28},
  {chart: "Universe today (observed)", element: "Oxygen", pct: 1},
  {chart: "Universe today (observed)", element: "All other elements", pct: 1}
]
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  const colors = {"Hydrogen": "#3fb7c7", "Helium": "#43a047", "Oxygen": "#fbc02d", "All other elements": "#e53935"};
  const charts = ["Early universe (predicted)", "Universe today (observed)"];
  const W = 640, H = 300, r = 105;
  const svg = d3.create("svg").attr("viewBox", `0 0 ${W} ${H}`).style("width", "100%").style("height", "auto").style("max-width", "640px").style("display", "block").style("margin", "auto");
  const pie = d3.pie().value(d => d.pct).sort(null);
  const arc = d3.arc().innerRadius(0).outerRadius(r);
  charts.forEach((ch, i) => {
    const g = svg.append("g").attr("transform", `translate(${160 + i * 320},${150})`);
    g.append("text").attr("y", -r - 18).attr("text-anchor", "middle").attr("font-size", 15).attr("font-weight", 700).attr("fill", "currentColor").text(ch);
    const arcs = pie(compositionData.filter(d => d.chart === ch));
    g.selectAll("path").data(arcs).join("path").attr("d", arc).attr("fill", d => colors[d.data.element]).attr("stroke", "white").attr("stroke-width", 1.5)
      .append("title").text(d => `${d.data.element}: ${d.data.pct}%`);
    g.selectAll("text.lbl").data(arcs.filter(d => d.data.pct >= 5)).join("text").attr("class", "lbl")
      .attr("transform", d => `translate(${d3.arc().innerRadius(r * 0.55).outerRadius(r * 0.55).centroid(d)})`)
      .attr("text-anchor", "middle").attr("font-size", 13).attr("font-weight", 700).attr("fill", "#0f172a")
      .text(d => `${d.data.element} ${d.data.pct}%`);
  });
  const legend = svg.append("g").attr("transform", `translate(${W / 2 - 230},${H - 14})`);
  Object.entries(colors).forEach(([k, c], i) => {
    legend.append("rect").attr("x", i * 120).attr("y", -10).attr("width", 12).attr("height", 12).attr("fill", c);
    legend.append("text").attr("x", i * 120 + 16).attr("y", 0).attr("font-size", 12).attr("fill", "currentColor").text(k === "All other elements" ? "Other (1%)" : k === "Oxygen" ? "Oxygen (1%)" : k);
  });
  return svg.node();
}
```

**What changed the percentages?** Stars! Inside stars, **nuclear fusion** turns hydrogen into helium (so hydrogen goes down a little and helium goes up), and it builds **heavier elements** like carbon and oxygen. When stars die, they spread those elements into space. Matter **changed form**, but it was not created or destroyed.

### Evidence 2: The light (cosmic microwave background)

Scientists predicted the leftover light from the early universe starting in the **1940s**. In **1965**, Arno Penzias and Robert Wilson found a faint **microwave** signal coming **equally from every direction** in the sky (the story in the packet's reading *Murmur of a Bang*). It is the **cosmic microwave background (CMB)**: the glow of the hot early universe, released when the first atoms formed (the packet's model says about 300,000 years after the beginning; modern measurements say about 380,000 years) and stretched by expansion into microwaves at about **2.7 K**.

<figure style="margin: 18px auto; max-width: 720px; text-align: center;">
  <img src="https://images-assets.nasa.gov/image/PIA16873/PIA16873~medium.jpg"
       alt="Oval all-sky map of the cosmic microwave background from the Planck mission, speckled with tiny blue (slightly cooler) and red-orange (slightly warmer) patches spread evenly across the whole sky"
       style="width: 100%; height: auto; border-radius: 12px; box-shadow: 0 6px 20px rgba(0,0,0,.25);">
  <figcaption style="margin-top: 8px; color: #64748b; font-size: .85em; font-style: italic; line-height: 1.4;">
    The cosmic microwave background mapped over the whole sky by ESA's Planck mission. The colors show differences of only about 1 part in 100,000. Credit: ESA and the Planck Collaboration / NASA.
  </figcaption>
</figure>

<div class="mind-blown">
🧠 About 1% of the "snow" on an old analog TV tuned between channels was the cosmic microwave background, the leftover light of the Big Bang.
</div>

### Bringing all the evidence together

Each piece of evidence supports the claim: *At the beginning of time, the universe was extremely small, hot, and dense but has been expanding ever since.* Try writing the reasoning for each yourself, then check.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Check your reasoning: Redshift in the spectra of galaxies
Galaxies' absorption lines are shifted toward longer (red) wavelengths, and farther galaxies are shifted more. By the Doppler effect, they are moving away from us, so the universe is expanding. Running the expansion backward, everything was once packed into a tiny, dense, hot state.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Check your reasoning: Microwave background radiation all over the universe
A hot, dense early universe would have glowed with intense light. Energy can't be destroyed, so that light should still exist, stretched by expansion. We detect it as microwaves (about 2.7 K) coming from every direction, which matches the prediction.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Check your reasoning: About 74% hydrogen, 25% helium, less than 2% heavier elements
Computational models of a hot, dense, expanding early universe predict 75% hydrogen and 25% helium. Matter can't be created or destroyed, so this mix should remain. Observations match, with the small differences explained by fusion in stars.
:::

- How do the **microwaves** compare with the visible light of the early universe? Does this match your prediction?
- How do these observations support the idea that **matter and energy are never created or destroyed**, but may change and move?
- Complete the **Evidence–Claim–Reasoning** table for all three pieces of evidence.

# Evaluate: Could There Be Other Earth-Like Planets?

::: {.evaluate-box}
## 🪐 From the Big Bang to Billions of Solar Systems

Our solar system has **8 planets**, and astronomers have found **multiple planets** around most of the other stars they have studied, so they think **most stars have planets**. With roughly **10²² to 10²⁴ stars** in the observable universe, how did they all form, and are other solar systems like ours?
:::

## Model of the Formation of the Universe

Step through the packet's *Big Bang Theory* model. The numbers are the ones printed in the packet's graphic; see the note below the chart for modern values.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
bbStages = [
  {n: 1, time: "10⁻⁴³ sec", sec: 1e-43, tempC: null, text: "The cosmos goes through a superfast \"inflation,\" expanding from the size of an atom to that of a grapefruit in a tiny fraction of a second."},
  {n: 2, time: "10⁻³² sec", sec: 1e-32, tempC: "10²⁷ °C", tempK: 1e27, text: "Post-inflation, the universe is a seething, hot soup of electrons, quarks, and other particles."},
  {n: 3, time: "10⁻⁶ sec", sec: 1e-6, tempC: "10¹³ °C", tempK: 1e13, text: "A rapidly cooling cosmos permits quarks to clump into protons and neutrons."},
  {n: 4, time: "3 min", sec: 180, tempC: "10⁸ °C", tempK: 1e8, text: "Still too hot to form into atoms, charged electrons and protons prevent light from shining; the universe is a superhot fog."},
  {n: 5, time: "300,000 yrs", sec: 300000 * 3.156e7, tempC: "10,000 °C", tempK: 10273, text: "Electrons combine with protons and neutrons to form atoms, mostly hydrogen and helium. Light can finally shine."},
  {n: 6, time: "1 billion yrs", sec: 1e9 * 3.156e7, tempC: "−200 °C", tempK: 73, text: "Gravity makes hydrogen and helium gas coalesce to form the giant clouds that will become galaxies; smaller clumps of gas collapse to form the first stars."},
  {n: 7, time: "15 billion yrs (present day)", sec: 15e9 * 3.156e7, tempC: "−270 °C", tempK: 3, text: "As galaxies cluster together under gravity, the first stars die and spew heavy elements into space; these will eventually form into new stars and planets."}
]
```

::: {.key-idea}
### 💡 The same processes everywhere

The same **physics** happened **everywhere** in the universe: the same expansion and cooling, the same **75% hydrogen / 25% helium**, the same **gravity** pulling gas into galaxies and stars, and the same stars making and scattering **heavy elements**. Spectra show that distant galaxies contain the **same elements** as our lab samples. So other galaxies and solar systems should have formed in **similar ways to ours**. With so many stars, it is likely that **Earth-like planets** exist elsewhere.
:::

# Chapter Summary

| Key Concept | Details |
|---|---|
| **Galaxy spectra** | Galaxies show the same absorption-line pattern as hydrogen and helium, but shifted toward red; farther galaxies are shifted more |
| **Wavelength and frequency** | Short wavelength = high frequency; long wavelength = low frequency |
| **Doppler effect (sound)** | A source moving toward you sounds higher (higher frequency); moving away sounds lower |
| **Doppler effect (light)** | Moving toward you → blueshift (shorter λ, higher f); moving away → redshift (longer λ, lower f) |
| **Colors** | Violet/blue = shortest λ, highest f; red = longest λ, lowest f (visible light ≈ 400–700 nm) |
| **Expanding universe** | All distant galaxies are redshifted, so they are moving apart: space is expanding (Hubble's Law: farther = faster) |
| **Big Bang** | Running expansion backward: about 13.7–13.8 billion years ago the universe was extremely small, hot, and dense |
| **Early elements** | Only hydrogen and helium formed: 75% H, 25% He by mass; today ~98% of matter is still H and He |
| **Cosmic microwave background** | The early universe's light, stretched about 1,100× into microwaves (~2.7 K), coming from every direction |
| **Conservation** | Matter and energy change form and move but are never created or destroyed; that's why we can still detect the Big Bang's matter and light |
| **Other Earths?** | The same processes acted everywhere, and there are 10²²–10²⁴ stars, most with planets |

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
function buildOriginQuiz(id, title, questions) {
  const outer = html`<div id="${id}" style="font-family:'Inter',sans-serif; max-width:720px; margin:18px auto;"></div>`;
  const header = html`<div style="background:linear-gradient(135deg,#667eea 0%,#764ba2 100%);color:#fff;border-radius:14px 14px 0 0;padding:18px 24px;">
    <div style="font-size:1.1em;font-weight:700;display:flex;align-items:center;gap:8px;"><span style="font-size:1.2em;">📝</span> ${title}</div>
    <div style="font-size:0.85em;opacity:0.85;margin-top:4px;">Select an answer for each question.</div>
  </div>`;
  const body = html`<div style="border:1.5px solid #c7d2fe;border-top:none;border-radius:0 0 14px 14px;overflow:hidden;background:#f8f9ff;padding:16px;"></div>`;
  questions.forEach((qq, qi) => {
    const card = document.createElement("div");
    card.style.cssText = "background:#fff;color:#1e1b4b;border-radius:12px;padding:16px 20px;margin-bottom:14px;box-shadow:0 2px 8px rgba(0,0,0,.08);";
    card.innerHTML = `<p style="font-weight:700;margin:0 0 10px;color:#1e1b4b;">${qi+1}. ${qq.q}</p>`;
    qq.options.forEach((opt, oi) => {
      const btn = document.createElement("button");
      btn.textContent = opt;
      btn.style.cssText = "display:block;width:100%;min-height:44px;text-align:left;padding:10px 14px;margin:6px 0;border:2px solid #e2e8f0;border-radius:8px;background:#fff;color:#1e1b4b;cursor:pointer;font-size:.95em;transition:border-color .2s,background .2s;";
      btn.onmouseover = () => { if(!card.dataset.answered){ btn.style.borderColor="#667eea";btn.style.background="#f0f0ff"; }};
      btn.onmouseout  = () => { if(!card.dataset.answered){ btn.style.borderColor="#e2e8f0";btn.style.background="#fff"; }};
      btn.onclick = () => {
        if(card.dataset.answered) return;
        card.dataset.answered = "true";
        card.querySelectorAll("button").forEach(b => {
          b.style.cursor="default"; b.onmouseover=null; b.onmouseout=null;
          b.style.borderColor="#e2e8f0"; b.style.background="#f8fafc"; b.style.color="#475569";
        });
        if(oi === qq.correct){
          btn.style.borderColor="#48bb78";btn.style.background="#f0fff4";btn.style.color="#276749";btn.style.fontWeight="700";
          fb.innerHTML = "✅ Correct! " + qq.explanation;
          fb.style.color="#276749";fb.style.background="#f0fff4";
        } else {
          btn.style.borderColor="#fc8181";btn.style.background="#fff5f5";btn.style.color="#9b2c2c";btn.style.fontWeight="700";
          const correctBtn = card.querySelectorAll("button")[qq.correct];
          correctBtn.style.borderColor="#48bb78";correctBtn.style.background="#f0fff4";correctBtn.style.color="#276749";correctBtn.style.fontWeight="700";
          fb.innerHTML = "❌ " + qq.explanation;
          fb.style.color="#9b2c2c";fb.style.background="#fff5f5";
        }
        fb.style.padding="10px 14px";fb.style.marginTop="8px";fb.style.borderRadius="8px";
      };
      card.appendChild(btn);
    });
    const fb = document.createElement("div");
    fb.style.cssText = "border-radius:8px;font-size:.9em;transition:all .3s;";
    card.appendChild(fb);
    body.appendChild(card);
  });
  outer.appendChild(header);
  outer.appendChild(body);
  return outer;
}
```
